text: Donjuan Triumphant, a bay stallion foaled on 24 March 2013 in Ireland, is a Thoroughbred racehorse known for excelling in sprint distances. Bred by Patrick Cosgrove and the Dream Ahead Syndicate, he was consigned to the Goffs sale in November 2013 and purchased for €58,000 by Lynn Lodge Stud; he later returned as a yearling at the Tattersalls "breeze-up" sale in early 2015, where he was bought for 30,000 guineas by Middleham Park Racing. Trained by Richard Fahey at Malton, North Yorkshire, his name references the title character in the novel *The Phantom of the Opera*. He is a member of the first crop of foals sired by Dream Ahead, a sprinter with wins in the Prix Morny, Middle Park Stakes, July Cup, Haydock Sprint Cup, and Prix de la Forêt, and his progeny includes Glass Slippers, Dream of Dreams, and Al Wukair. His dam, Mathuna, won on her debut but failed to win in eight subsequent starts and was descended from Mariella, who won the Premio Roma, and is a half-sister to Sagaro. Donjuan Triumphant made his racecourse debut on 20 June 2015 at Redcar, finishing second by a head to Receding Waves, and sustained narrow defeats at Ayr, Carlisle, and Haydock before winning his first race at Ayr two weeks later by three and a quarter lengths with apprentice jockey Jack Garritty. He then won the Listed Rockingham Stakes at York on 10 October by one and a half lengths from Dhamaan and the Group 2 Critérium de Maisons-Laffitte in France on 11 October by five and a half lengths after taking the lead 200 metres from the finish. In 2016, he finished second to Quiet Reflection in the Temple Stakes and behind her in the Commonwealth Cup at Royal Ascot, and placed second to Signs of Blessing in the Group 1 Prix Maurice de Gheest at Deauville. He failed to win in the following races, including the Haydock Sprint Cup and the British Champions Sprint Stakes, and competed in minor races on synthetic tracks. In 2017, he was bought privately by Vichai Srivaddhanaprabha and transferred to Andrew Balding’s stable at Kingsclere, carrying King Power Racing’s blue and white colours. He won a minor race at Haydock in August 2017 after a lengthy absence, beating five opponents by one and a quarter lengths, and later ran in the Ayr Gold Cup, which was moved to Haydock due to waterlogging, winning by a short head. In 2018, he finished eighth in the British Champions Sprint Stakes at Ascot. On 10 November 2018, he won the Listed Wentworth Stakes at Doncaster on soft ground by a head, ridden by James Doyle and starting as a 2/1 favourite. After Vichai Srivaddhanaprabha’s death in the 2018 Leicester helicopter crash, Andrew Balding reflected on the tragedy and praised Donjuan Triumphant’s toughness and love for soft ground. In 2019, he made a strong comeback, finishing fourth in the Haydock Sprint Cup and third in the British Champions Sprint Stakes, and was rated 118 in the 2019 World's Best Racehorse Rankings, making him the 78th best racehorse globally. He retired at the end of 2019 and began his career as a breeding stallion at Haras de la Barbottiere in Sablé-sur-Sarthe in 2020 at a fee of €4,000.
